edges.description: Perceived agency fell after two weeks of delegation.
People who chose what to delegate felt more in control.
Approving drafts kept perceived agency near baseline.
Oversight matters more than the amount of delegation.
Delegating routine tasks lowered perceived agency.
When people choose what to delegate, delegation can increase their sense of control.
Routing cut inference cost by about forty percent.
